name: @maviapi/mcp

tools.name: search_apis
tools.description: Find a ready-made maviapi API for a website or topic, e.g. "hotels", "flights", "booking.com" or "turkish news". maviapi turns websites that have no official API into structured JSON endpoints, and monitors and repairs them when the site changes. Leave `query` empty to list every API. Next step: get_api, to see an API's endpoints and parameters.

query.description: Website, domain, or topic to look for. Empty lists everything.

tools.name: get_api
tools.description: Show one maviapi API's endpoints: what each returns, its parameters (required ones marked), the fields in the response, and whether each endpoint is working right now. Also lists endpoints that are being built. Accepts the API slug from search_apis, or the site's domain (e.g. "airbnb.com"). Read this before call_api. If the API lacks what you need, request_endpoint adds an endpoint to it.

api.description: API slug (e.g. "booking") or the site's domain.

tools.name: call_api
tools.description: Fetch live, structured JSON from a website through a maviapi endpoint. `api` is the API slug (or domain), `endpoint` the endpoint name or path from get_api, and `params` its parameters, path parameters such as {id} included. List endpoints return 10 results unless you pass `limit`; page with `offset`. Each successful call uses one maviapi credit.

api.description: API slug (e.g. "booking") or the site's domain.

params.description: Endpoint parameters, as listed by get_api.

version.description: Call this version of the API instead of the live one (see get_changelog). Rarely needed.

tools.name: create_api
tools.description: Start an API draft for a website that no catalog API covers. maviapi's build agent studies the site and builds a JSON API from a plain-language description. This returns a request_id at once; follow it with get_build_status. Build completion does not publish the API. Use your own account and key to review and publish the draft in the dashboard. With the shared demo key each network gets 3 free builds per 30 days.

description.description: The data wanted from the site, as specific as you can: pages, fields, filters. E.g. "front-page stories with title, url, points, comment count and author".

build_anyway.description: Build even though the catalog already has an API for this site (it lacks what you need).

tools.name: get_build_status
tools.description: Where a build started with create_api or request_endpoint is: its phase, each endpoint with its test results or what went wrong, and what the build said last. A finished build is not public until it is published (publish_request, or the owner in the dashboard). Pass `wait_seconds` (up to 50) and the call returns as soon as something changes, so you can follow a build without sleeping. With the shared demo key it reports the plain build status only.

request_id.description: The request_id create_api or request_endpoint returned.

wait_seconds.description: Hold the call up to this many seconds (max 50) until the build's state changes.

tools.name: request_endpoint
tools.description: Add one endpoint to an API that already exists, or a changed version of one of its endpoints. Use it when get_api shows the API lacks the data, or an endpoint returns the wrong thing. Existing endpoints never change: a change ships as a new endpoint beside the old one (e.g. /search-v2). Without `confirm` nothing is built: the tool answers with the endpoint as it would be built, for the user to agree to. Call it again with the same arguments and `confirm: true` to start the build (about half an hour). One build of an API runs at a time: a request made while another is building waits in line and starts on its own. Needs an API key with the requests:write permission. Follow the build with get_build_status.

api.description: API slug (e.g. "booking") or the site's domain.

description.description: What the endpoint returns, as specific as you can: the page it reads, the fields per record, the parameters. E.g. "The reviews of one hotel, newest first: author, rating, date, text. Parameter: hotel id."

path.description: For a new endpoint: its path, lowercase with dashes, no parameters in it. E.g. "/reviews" or "/hotel-photos".

change.description: For a changed version of an existing endpoint: that endpoint's name or path, e.g. "/search". Use instead of `path`.

confirm.description: true starts the build. Leave it out to preview first.

tools.name: list_requests
tools.description: The API and endpoint requests made with this account, newest first, with their status. Filter by `api` (slug) or `status` (queued, building, deploying, published, failed). Needs an API key with a request permission.

api.description: Only requests for this API slug.

tools.name: send_request_message
tools.description: Say something to the build of a request, in plain words: add detail, ask it to fix or drop an endpoint that failed, or to try again after a failure (e.g. "fix /reviews", "also return the review date", "try again"). Returns the build's answer. Needs an API key with the requests:write permission.

request_id.description: The request_id from request_endpoint or create_api.

tools.name: call_draft
tools.description: Call an endpoint of a request's draft before it is published, to check it returns the right data. Only endpoints get_build_status shows as ready answer. Draft calls cost no credits. Needs an API key with a request permission.

request_id.description: The request_id from request_endpoint or create_api.

endpoint.description: The endpoint path as get_build_status lists it, e.g. "/reviews".

tools.name: publish_request
tools.description: Make a finished request live: every endpoint that passed its checks becomes part of the public API. Publishing changes what everyone who calls the API gets, so do it only when the user asked for it. Works once get_build_status says the request is ready. Needs an API key with the requests:publish permission.

request_id.description: The request_id from request_endpoint or create_api.

tools.name: cancel_request
tools.description: Stop the build that is running for a request. What was built before stays as it was. Needs an API key with the requests:write permission.

request_id.description: The request_id from request_endpoint or create_api.

tools.name: report_endpoint_issue
tools.description: Tell maviapi that an endpoint that exists returns the wrong thing: it fails, comes back empty, or repeats the same page. Use this instead of asking for a changed version when the endpoint is simply broken: the fix lands on the endpoint itself, for everyone. maviapi replays the call at once and then runs its own check of the endpoint. If that check fails too the report is confirmed and the endpoint is queued for repair; if not (a fault only certain parameters show, a repeated page, wrong values) a person on the team reads the report. A report's status is confirmed, fixed or received. Report what you saw: maviapi takes a report of an API only from an account that has called it with its own key, so make the failing call with call_api first, then pass its `params` here. Without `endpoint` and `description` it lists the reports made with this key. Needs an API key with the requests:write permission (any request permission to list).

api.description: API slug (e.g. "booking") or the site's domain.

endpoint.description: The endpoint's name or path, e.g. "/restaurants".

description.description: What is wrong, in a sentence or two: what you asked for, what came back, what you expected. E.g. "page=2 returns the same 30 restaurants as page 1."

params.description: The parameters of a call that shows the fault, e.g. {"geo": "187147", "page": 2}.

tools.name: get_key_info
tools.description: What the configured API key may do: its permissions, the account's plan and remaining credits, and the limits that apply. Check it before starting something that needs a permission or uses credits. Needs an API key with a request permission.

tools.name: get_changelog
tools.description: Every version of an API, newest first: which is live, when it was built, and what changed (endpoints added or removed, fields changed). Use it when an endpoint behaves differently than before, or to pick a version for call_api's `version`.

api.description: API slug (e.g. "booking") or the site's domain.

instructions:
maviapi gives you live, structured JSON from websites that have no official API (travel, e-commerce, news, events, finance and more).
Workflow: search_apis to find an API for a site or topic, get_api to read its endpoints and parameters, then call_api to fetch data.
If no API covers the site you need, create_api builds one (about half an hour; follow it with get_build_status).
If an API exists but lacks an endpoint, or you need one to behave differently, request_endpoint adds one: preview it, let the user agree, start it with confirm: true, follow it with get_build_status (wait_seconds), try it with call_draft, and publish_request when the user wants it live.
If an endpoint is simply broken (it fails, comes back empty, or repeats the same page), report_endpoint_issue with the params of the failing call: maviapi replays it and checks the endpoint itself. A fault its own check confirms is repaired in place; the rest are read by a person.
Starting a build and publishing change things for the user: do them when the user asked, not on your own.
